The Celtic harp, also called the Irish harp, is a triangular-framed chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 322.221, traditional to the Celtic regions of north-west Europe, with local names in Ireland, Scotland, Wales and Brittany. Its resonating box is usually carved from a single piece of wood, often willow, and also alder or poplar; the strings are brass or iron, and modern experiments have tried silver, gold and others. The player plucks with long fingernails, which takes years of practice. The metal-strung harps of Ireland and Scotland are traditionally associated with the Gaelic aristocracy: early Irish law had poets and cruit players seated with the nobles at banquets, while in Wales the instrument was played by professional musicians.
凱爾特豎琴為西北歐凱爾特地區的三角框豎琴，早期歷史有爭議；蓋爾世界早期弦樂器稱c: The Celtic harp is the triangular-framed harp of the Celtic regions of north-west Europe; its early history is disputed. The early string instrument of the Gaelic world was called cruit, and the triangular-framed harp may have taken over that name in Scotland. A triangular-framed harp already appears on eighth-century Pictish stone carvings, and it later spread to Anglo-Saxon England, the Highlands and Ireland. Clear images appear in Ireland from the late eleventh century, and Welsh documents mention it frequently in the twelfth. Surviving Gaelic harps from the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries have a low head; the instrument declined by the late eighteenth century, a new gut-strung harp appeared in the nineteenth, the Scottish cultural revival promoted the new harp in the 1890s, and modern strings are mostly nylon.
凱爾特豎琴的共鳴箱通常由整根木料雕成，常見柳木，現存琴亦見桤木與楊木。愛爾蘭與蘇: The resonating box of a Celtic harp is usually carved from a single piece of wood, commonly willow; surviving instruments also use alder and poplar. Traditional Irish and Scottish harps mostly use metal strings, low-quality brass being common in the 1500s; modern experiments also use copper alloy, silver, gold, soft iron and brass, while modern harps mostly use nylon. Early Welsh harps have horsehair and gut strings, a wooden frame, an animal-skin soundboard, and pegs of wood or bone, some with L-shaped wooden pegs. The pillar is reinforced, the neck carries thick brass bands on both sides, and the arm is studded with brass bands and fitted with tapered brass tuning pins.
凱爾特豎琴音色溫潤優雅，具有獨特的穿透力與詩意感。其高音區明亮清晰，如同晶瑩的水: The Celtic harp's timbre is warm and elegant, with a distinctive penetration and a poetic quality. The top register is bright and clear, like drops of water; the middle is warm and soft and full of song; the bass resonates deeply with a bleak, open feeling. The vibration of the strings produces rich overtones through the resonating box, giving a timbre of sweeping layers. Compared with the ornate refinement of the classical harp, the Celtic harp is rawer and plainer; compared with the piano, its tone is warmer and softer, without the hard edge. The natural decay of a plucked string creates a dreamy, drifting atmosphere, especially suited to folk feeling and quiet meditation.
坐姿將琴靠於肩上或置於身前。將樂器穩定持於身前。左手負責按弦或改變有效弦長以控制: Sit and rest the harp on your shoulder or hold it in front of you. Hold the instrument steady in front of you. The left hand stops the strings, or changes the sounding length, to control pitch, and the right hand sets the strings vibrating. A chordophone works by the vibration of the string being amplified through a resonating body. Pluck the strings with the fingertips or a plectrum, watching the angle and force of contact.
